content.comment_body: Hello, A similar question was raised before, but I believe my issue is different. I have a new [article_no] device that I can't access. It’s connected to my router and should have a fixed IP of 192.168.1.4. Here's what I've tried: - Using a network scan tool, the [product_name] sometimes appears at the expected IP address, but then disappears. - Pinging the IP from the command prompt usually times out, though occasionally I get a response. - Attempting to open a socket connection in Java on port 102 doesn't work. - In [product_name] Soft Comfort under Tools > Options > Interface, I added the IP with subnet mask 255.255.255.0 and left the gateway blank. Status is 'No' when I press detect. - Transferring from PC to [product_name] using [product_name] Soft results in "cannot access the IP address 192.168.1.4." Each time I try to connect, the lights near the RJ45 port on the [product_name] light up, so there is some activity. I haven't connected the ground cable next to the RJ45 on the [product_name], but I don't think that’s causing the IP issue. Any ideas why the [product_name] seems to keep losing its IP or why I can't connect?

Hi, 1. Try connecting to the [product_name] directly without using a router. If that works, the problem likely lies in the settings. 2. Note that the port used for connecting [product_name] Soft Comfort to the [product_name] is 10001, not 102 as with other [product_name] models. Hope this helps.
Hello [user_name], I had a similar issue recently. Open CMD on Windows and type IPCONFIG. If there is more than one IP in the results, let me know.

Hello [user_name], When transferring a program to the [product_name], make sure the same IP address is set in [product_name] Soft Comfort under 'Tools > Options > Interface' (for example, 192.168.1.4) as well as 'Tools > Ethernet Connections'. The setting in 'Tools > Options > Interface' is important for transferring and detecting the device. If 'Tools > Ethernet Connections' has a different IP (for example, 192.168.1.6), after loading the program into the [product_name] device, [product_name] Soft Comfort will display "Overwrite IP address setting in device". Clicking OK will set the device to use the IP from 'Tools > Ethernet Connections', and you won’t be able to access the device through the other IP. This IP mismatch often causes problems accessing the [product_name] device. If you have further questions, feel free to ask. Best regards, [user_name]

Thanks for the suggestions. I managed to set up the IP for both the [product_name] and the PC and connected directly without the router. Now, I can connect, and I’m also able to use port 10001 to start, stop, and check IO status with Java. However, it's still unclear how to write to the [product_name]—the examples from the library don’t work. I uploaded a test program with a network input at address 100 bit 0, but reading or writing doesn't work. Does anyone have a working sample of a [product_name] Soft Comfort program and a corresponding library test that reliably functions?
Hello [user_name], Did you try pinging the [product_name] from your PC directly? What results do you get?
Figured it out—thanks for everyone’s help.

analysis.insight_summary: The main issue was unstable Ethernet connectivity and inconsistent IP address recognition between a PC and a [product_name] module ([article_no]). Users highlighted that mismatches between software settings for IP addresses are a common cause for problems. They also clarified the different ports used by various [product_name] products/software, and shared troubleshooting steps like connecting directly instead of via a router. Ultimately, setting matching IP configurations resolved the connectivity problem. Minor issues with programming interfaces were noted, emphasizing that network and device settings must be coordinated for reliable operation.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect stable and predictable Ethernet connection between their PC and the [product_name] module, simple setup for fixed IP addresses, and smoothly transferring and working with programs on the device, without needing advanced troubleshooting or detailed manual configuration.
